title: Lesson 2 Quiz: Economic Growth and Productivity
description: A short quiz to check what you learned in this lesson. Submitting it completes the lesson's quiz requirement, and your score is recorded separately.

history.note: AI-written question draft. Not reviewed or approved by a human (admin); do not give to students.

Comprehensive audit: difficulty tags matched to cognitive demand (q2 beginner, q4 intermediate); l2-q5 distractors that contradicted the stem replaced with plausible misconceptions. Not reviewed or approved by a human.

questions.prompt: In which situation does labor productivity (real output per hour worked) rise?

choices.text: Workers trained on new software finish more orders in each hour than before
A firm hires more workers, and output per worker stays the same as before
Workers put in more hours, and the firm's total output stays the same
The price of the firm's product rises, while its output per hour stays the same

questions.prompt: Hypothetical example: Country S (1) builds a new rail line to its ports, (2) pays for nurses to complete an advanced training course, and (3) has its factories adopt a better method of scheduling production. Which classification of these three changes is correct?
Hypothetical example: Country T's real GDP per capita grows at a steady 2.5% per year. Using the rule of 70, about how many years will it take to double? (Enter a number only, in years.)

Hypothetical example: Country U's real GDP is $80 billion and grows 4% per year, compounded, for 3 years. What is real GDP after 3 years, in billions of dollars? Round to two decimal places, and round only at the final step. (Enter a number only.)
Hypothetical example: Over one year, Country V's real GDP grew 5% while the total amount of raw materials its economy used fell 2%. How does this outcome relate to SDG target 8.4?

choices.text: It is relative decoupling, because material use grew more slowly than output
Output grew while material use fell, which is the decoupling target 8.4 describes
It is not decoupling, because target 8.4 is about emissions rather than materials
Labor productivity fell, because the economy used fewer materials for each worker
